chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammām ibn Suhayl Al-Iskāfī narrated to me from Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Mālik Al-Fazārī, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Rawāsi, from someone who narrated to him, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever goes to (the Ziyārah of) Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) and performs Wuďū and Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates, does not raise a foot or place a foot down without Allāh registering for him a Hajj and an ‘Umrah.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Ghusl in the Euphrates before visiting Imam Husain?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith underscores the unique sanctity of the Euphrates (Al-Furat) as a purifying medium linked to the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the Shia tradition of associating specific rivers with the Imams' spiritual authority. It elevates the physical act of Ziyarah into a continuous state of worship, where mere movement in ritual purity accrues the reward of major pilgrimages, emphasizing the transformative power of proximity to Imam Husayn (a.s.).

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Hammām ibn Suhayl Al-Iskāfi narrated to me from Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Mālik Al-Fazāri, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Rawāsi, from someone who narrated to him, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Those who go to (the Ziyārah of) Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) and perform Wuďū and Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates (River) do not raise their foot or place it down without Allāh registering a Hajj and an ‘Umrah for them.
